The case statement matches only exact trimmed lines, so inline placeholders like "- {{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}" won't match and will pass through unsubstituted.

  WHY: Inline unresolved placeholders (e.g., "text {{PLACEHOLDER}} text") will silently pass validation and be sent to the LLM as raw template syntax instead of being caught as errors.

- scripts/render_prompt.sh: Lines 46-65 (while loop with case-based substitution) | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: When a placeholder line is matched, the replacement is emitted via printf without preserving the original line's leading indentation. The code trims the line to check the case match, then outputs only the raw replacement variable (e.g., printf '%s\n' "${WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION_LINE}"), discarding the whitespace prefix that `line` carried.
  WHY: Any prompt template that places a placeholder on an indented line (e.g., nested markdown lists, indented instruction blocks) will lose its formatting structure after rendering, producing malformed prompts sent to the LLM.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh: Lines 67-81 (unresolved-placeholder validation grep checks) | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  PROBLEM: The three grep checks use anchored patterns like `^[[:space:]]*\{\{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION\}\}[[:space:]]*$` which only detect unresolved placeholders when they are the sole content on a line. Inline placeholders (e.g., `Reminder: {{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}} applies`) are not matched by any of the three grep patterns.
  WHY: Unresolved inline placeholders pass validation silently and are sent to the LLM as literal template text, causing the model to see raw {{NAME}} strings instead of the intended substituted values.
